cards: Hammurabi was a king of Babylon who reigned c. 1792–1750 BCE and built the Babylonian Empire across Mesopotamia.
r. c. 1792–1750 BCE · Ancient Near East
Shamshi-Adad I was an Amorite ruler who reigned c. 1808–1776 BCE and built a kingdom across northern Mesopotamia, including the city of Assur.
r. c. 1808–1776 BCE · Ancient Near East
Amenemhat IV was the penultimate king of the Twelfth Dynasty of Egypt, reigning for about nine years in the late nineteenth century BCE.
r. c. 1786–1777 BCE · Egypt & North Africa
Neferhotep I was a king of the Thirteenth Dynasty of Egypt who reigned for about eleven years in the mid-eighteenth century BCE, one of the best-attested rulers of the dynasty.
Sobekhotep IV was a king of the Thirteenth Dynasty of Egypt in the mid-eighteenth century BCE, brother of Neferhotep I, and one of the most powerful rulers of the dynasty.
Sobekneferu was the last ruler of the Twelfth Dynasty of Egypt, reigning for nearly four years in the late nineteenth century BCE.
r. c. 1777–1773 BCE · Egypt & North Africa
Abba-El I was king of Yamhad, with its capital at Aleppo, in the 18th century BCE.
Nehesy was a king of the Fourteenth Dynasty of Egypt, which ruled the eastern Nile Delta in the Second Intermediate Period, and is the best-attested ruler of that line.
fl. c. 1705 BCE · Egypt & North Africa
Piyusti was a king of Hatti in central Anatolia in the 18th century BCE, ruling from Hattusa.
Yarim-Lim was a prince of Yamhad and brother of King Abba-El I, who in the 18th century BCE received Alalakh and founded a dependent dynasty ruling the kingdom of Mukish under Aleppo.
